sentences.text: Tratayenia was a medium-sized meat-eating dinosaur that reached a length of about 8 meters.
This predator likely used large claws on its hands to catch prey, a feature shared by other members of its group.
Its spine shows a unique structure where the front joint plates are rectangular with edges meeting at nearly a right angle.
The animal possessed five vertebrae in its sacrum, which is the typical number for theropods.
Another distinct trait involves the rectangular shape of the precoracoid processes, where the front and lower borders converge.
Tratayenia stands as the biggest carnivore discovered in the Bajo de la Carpa Formation.
The nearly right-angled convergence of its front vertebral joint plates is a rare anatomical adaptation.
The single known species, Tratayenia rosalesi, was officially named in March 2018 after a partial skeleton found in 2006.
The main specimen, cataloged as MUCPv 1162, was unearthed by technician Diego Rosales at a site in the Bajo de la Carpa Formation.
Currently, the Paleobiology Database records only this one fossil occurrence for the genus.
The creature inhabited a dry landscape shaped by rivers and wind-blown sediments.
It shared its home with other theropods, ornithopods like Mahuidacursor, and massive titanosaurian sauropods.
Contemporary life included lizards, turtles, snakes, birds, crocodylomorphs, and dinosaurs such as Viavenator and Traukutitan.
Tratayenia is placed within the family Megaraptoridae.
Researchers Porfiri and colleagues assigned it to a broad, unresolved group of megaraptorids, supporting the view that these animals are coelurosaurs outside of Tyrannosauroidea.
The final classification relies on a strict consensus derived from averaging the twelve most parsimonious evolutionary trees.
Living during the Santonian age of the Late Cretaceous, this animal existed roughly 83 million years ago in what is now South America.
More precisely, its time range falls between 85.7 and 83.6 million years ago.
The evolutionary connections of megaraptorans, including Tratayenia, to other theropods remain a subject of intense disagreement among scientists.
One theory proposes that these dinosaurs are carnosaurs, distantly related to Allosaurus but more closely linked to Neovenator and carcharodontosaurids.
Another popular idea suggests they are basal tyrannosauroids, part of the coelurosaur lineage that also includes crested proceratosaurids and famous tyrannosaurids like Tyrannosaurus.
